voice.text: A submarine dives all the way to the bottom of the ocean. [pause] What does it find down there? Tap your guess: flat sand — or mountains and canyons?

Dive with the submarine! The ocean floor is not flat sand — it has <emphasis>shape</emphasis>, like the land. [pause] First the shallow continental shelf, just off the beach. Then the steep slope — down, down. Then the huge flat abyssal plain. And then — a trench! A canyon deeper than any mountain is tall. [pause] Underwater ridges and lone seamounts rise from the plain.

As we sink, the light fades. The top is the <emphasis>sunlight zone</emphasis> — bright, warm, crowded with life. Below it, the <emphasis>twilight zone</emphasis> — dim and cold. And at the bottom, the <emphasis>midnight zone</emphasis> — pitch dark and icy, all year long. [pause] And every drop, top to bottom, is salty. Never drink it!

Now feel the water move! The waves on top? <emphasis>Wind</emphasis> makes those — the harder it blows, the bigger they roll. [pause] And the slow rise and fall of the whole sea at the shore — the tides — that is the <emphasis>moon's pull</emphasis>, twice a day. You learned that with our neighbor, the moon!

And deep inside the ocean, the water travels in <emphasis>currents</emphasis> — giant rivers flowing in the sea. The Gulf Stream is one: it carries warm southern water up along our coast and across the sea, warming faraway shores. [pause] The ocean is never, ever still.

Who lives here? Where sunlight reaches, life crowds in — coral reefs packed with fish, like a busy city. [pause] But the deep dark is not empty! Down in the midnight zone live specialists, like the anglerfish — it dangles its own glowing lure, to catch dinner in the blackness.

And what feeds them all? <emphasis>Plankton</emphasis> — clouds of tiny drifting living things. Plankton is the ocean's grass: little fish eat plankton, big fish eat little fish. [pause] Food webs don't stop at the beach — they keep going, all the way down.
Label the dive! The submarine goes from the beach to the deepest deep: shelf, slope, abyssal plain, trench. Tap the next stop.
Who lives where? Match each resident to its zone — sunlight, twilight, or midnight.
What moves the water? Waves, tides, currents — each has its own cause. Tap the true one.
Surfacing! Great dive, explorer. [pause] Now show what you know.
Not quite. Shore to deepest, the dive goes: shelf, then slope, then abyssal plain, then trench.
Not quite. Follow the light: bright creatures live where the sun reaches. Glowing creatures live where it never does.
Not quite. The deep dark is not empty — special animals live there, and some bring their own light.
Not quite. Wind makes the waves. The moon makes the tides. Don't swap them!
Not quite. The ocean is never still — currents flow through it like rivers in the sea.
Not quite. Plankton is alive — and almost every ocean food web starts with it, like grass on land.
What is the deep ocean floor like?
Deep down, ocean water is…
Only the waves on top move — the rest of the ocean stands still. True?
What lives in the pitch-dark midnight zone?
Why is plankton called the ocean's grass?
<soft>You know the deep!</soft> [pause] Well done, explorer.
Good try! Let's ride the dive once more.
Lesson done! Go find one deep-sea creature in your research.
